headline: Tail edges to 19% as NQ extends to a third record 31,317.25 and holds near the extreme, with the 10-year at 5.35% pressing against the equity bid
body:
The prior hour published Tail at 18% on a break through the rejected 31,254.75 high and a new record at 31,280.00. That upward extension has continued rather than stalled.

NQZ26 has printed a further record high of 31,317.25 and the last verified quote is 31,298.00 at 18:16:31Z, up 236.25 points or 0.76% on the 31,061.75 prior close, against a 31,059.00 open and a day range of 30,957.50 to 31,317.25. Price is holding roughly 19 points beneath the extreme. The cash index confirms it: NASDAQ-100 is 31,050.73 at 18:26:32Z, up 242.79 points or 0.79% on a 30,807.93 prior close, about 11 points under its own 31,061.94 session high. The S&P 500 at 7,778.11 is effectively sitting on its 7,778.64 high.

This is now the third consecutive new extreme of the session, each following a retracement that failed to hold. Repeated extension after failed pullbacks, with price pinned near the high into the afternoon, is the pattern that most reliably precedes a path which denies meaningful mean reversion. It is why Tail moves up again.

Four things keep it inside the low band. First, the retracements have been genuine: the 62.50-point pullback to 31,192.25 earlier in the session is real two-way trade, not the shallow or absent structure that defines a pathological path. Second, the magnitude is modest. A 0.76% day with a 359.75-point range is an orderly grind higher, not violent directional repricing. Third, volatility is decaying as price rises: VIX is 15.60 at 18:10:46Z, up 1.89% on the day but down from a 16.38 session high, which is not the behaviour of a market pricing a disorderly path. Fourth, and most important, the cross-asset stack is conflicting rather than aligned. The 10-year note yield is 5.35%, up about seven basis points and near 24-year highs, with the 2-year at 4.86%; the CBOE 10-year yield index corroborates at 5.34 against a 5.28 prior close. Oil is lower, with WTI at 89.88 dollars down 1.35% and Brent at 100.78 dollars down 1.44%. A record equity print against a rising long end and falling crude is a divergence that belongs in Stress and Confidence, not in Tail.

The driver of the yield move is identifiable. September ISM Services printed at 54.9% at 14:00Z with the Prices Index at 74.0%, its highest since July 2022, which pushed the long end higher even after Friday's soft 29,000 payroll print had trimmed October hike expectations. Breadth has meanwhile broadened through the afternoon: the Dow has turned positive at 51,305.14, up 0.25%, having been down 0.13% at midday, and SMH is 633.39 dollars, up 0.44% against 0.17% earlier. Broader participation slightly raises the amplifier count, but Nasdaq still leads the Dow roughly three to one, so this remains a megacap and AI-led advance. Part of the index strength is also idiosyncratic rather than macro: PTC is up 34.6% on Schneider Electric's 22.6 billion dollar all-cash bid at 205 dollars a share, a 42% premium, and RXO is up 22.5% on a 5.8 billion dollar C.H. Robinson agreement. Deal-driven single-stock moves do not create index-level one-way structure.

The narrow evidence-based window is power hour into the cash close, 19:00Z to 20:15Z. That is where a session already at its extreme could convert into late-session continuation, and it is the only hour of the 24 modelled where published Tail reaches the watch band. After the 20:00Z close, index liquidity drains and the published path falls to a 10% trough in the pre-Asia hours.

The shared Finviz context file was read and not used. Its generatedAt is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly six days old, and its collectionStatus is partial, so it is well outside the 90-minute freshness bound and cannot support current cross-asset evidence. All levels cited above come from independently fetched primary sources instead, which is why Confidence stays at 88% despite the missing shared feed.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 18:00Z, Claude published Tail between 3% and 18% and Stress between 46% and 71%, with every hour mapping to EA_ON and green. Tail sat at 3% through the Oct 4 US evening, rose into a 12% to 15% overnight band, troughed at 6% during the European morning, and then oscillated between 7% and 18% through the US session as successive session highs were tested, rejected and finally exceeded. Stress declined steadily from 71% late on Oct 4 to 46% by midday Oct 5 before firming back to 52% as the long end pressed higher. Dominant mode was normal overnight, briefly trend-down at 10:00Z, mixed through most of the US morning, and trend-up at 14:00Z and 17:00Z. One hour, 06:00Z on Oct 5, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than filled in.
outlookSummary: The published path treats power hour into the US cash close as the one window where current evidence supports watch-band risk. Tail peaks at 20% at 19:00Z, the only slot of the 24 that maps to WATCH and yellow, then returns to 19% across the 20:00Z close before falling through 15% and 11% as the cash session ends and liquidity drains. The overnight trough is 10% in the pre-Asia and Tokyo-open hours, with Stress bottoming at 44%. Risk rebuilds gradually through the Asian and European sessions, with mode shifting to mixed at the 07:00Z European open, and the published path then tracks the Oct 6 US calendar: 14% across the 12:15Z ADP and 12:30Z balance of trade block, a 17% secondary peak at 13:00Z covering Fed Williams at 13:05Z and the 13:30Z cash open, 16% through Fed Bowman at 14:45Z, and 13% into the 17:00Z 3-year note auction. Every slot other than 19:00Z stays inside the low band. Forward values are conditional risk, not an assertion that any future price path has been observed.
